name: 3D agent monitor: critique, approach, wiring plan
about: Critiques the NEXUS 3D mock-ups, builds improved ones in a new folder, recommends how to build the 3D agent monitor and writes the wiring plan. Documents and mock-ups only: no wiring is implemented.

steps.title: Critique the seven NEXUS 3D mock-ups
steps.goal:
Wyarden is getting a 3D view of what coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, Antigravity) are doing, live, in any VS Code workspace. The owner clicks objects in 3D; every change to information happens in ordinary VS Code UI, never in the scene. It must show the tools an agent uses, the resources it uses (files, URLs, context) as a separate class, and each call to an MCP server. It runs beside the agents, so it draws only on change and its cost is measured.

This plan makes documents and mock-ups only: implement no wiring. The repository is public: commit no email address, account name, machine name or absolute local path.

Your part: critique the existing 3D mock-ups.

They are in the Entridir repository at C:/Users/rober/Documents/Dev Stuff/Entridir/Entridir. It is read only: never edit, build or delete anything there. These are the only copies.
- nexus-3d/ui-concepts/nexus-lattice-29d4d1/ is the NEXUS lattice. The owner accepted its look by eye.
- nexus-3d/ui-concepts/nexus-worlds-29d4d1/ holds six worlds: Circuit City, Orbital Mechanics, Glasshouse, Synapse, Event Horizon, Signal Terrain.
- nexus-3d/ui-concepts/signal-house-29d4d1/ is 2D and out of scope, except for ideas worth borrowing.
For comparison, the versions that were wired to real data: ui/lattice*.js, godot/looks/*.gd, nexus-3d/src/lattice.ts, and the screenshots under docs/verification/ and nexus-3d/docs/evidence/.

Do this:
1. Run each of the seven. In its folder, node serve.js serves on loopback only (port 4320 for the lattice, 4321 for the worlds; pass another port as the first argument if it is busy). Stop it when you are done. Save one screenshot of each under docs/monitor-3d/img/before/ with headless Edge or Chrome; test/compile-webview-cdp.js shows how this repository drives one. If no browser runs, say so in the document and work from the code.
2. Write docs/monitor-3d/01-mockup-critique.md:
- The verdict in five lines at the top.
- A table of what each mock-up is: renderer, data model, visual encoding, interaction.
- Weaknesses ranked by severity against the needs above, each with evidence (file and line, or a screenshot).
- A table rating how well each of the seven concepts can carry agents, tools, resources and MCP servers as visibly separate classes, with its main flaw.
- The concept to build on, and whether the NEXUS lattice should stay as a second look, with reasons.
- A numbered list of improvements, each marked must-have or nice-to-have, each concrete enough to build and to test. A later step builds from this list.
- What to carry over from Entridir's Godot looks (godot/looks/look.gd, godot/README.md).

Check these starting points yourself; do not trust them. Both mock-ups draw with a hand-written Canvas 2D projection in a requestAnimationFrame loop that never stops. model.js is the same file in both: 12 node types, 40 nodes, 52 edges, 32 scripted events. There is no file, URL or MCP server class. A tool and a task share one shape. Status colour replaces type colour. Layouts move existing nodes when the count changes. Labels collide past about 40 nodes. An earlier read judged Glasshouse's fixed floors plus Circuit City's per-agent columns the best base.

Change nothing outside docs/monitor-3d/.
steps.reply: the commit id, the five-line verdict, the concept you chose to build on, how many screenshots you saved (or why none), and the document's path

steps.title: Inventory the live signals for tools, resources and MCP calls
steps.goal:
Wyarden is getting a 3D view of what coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, Antigravity) are doing, live, in any VS Code workspace. The owner clicks objects in 3D; every change to information happens in ordinary VS Code UI, never in the scene. It must show the tools an agent uses, the resources it uses (files, URLs, context) as a separate class, and each call to an MCP server. It runs beside the agents, so it draws only on change and its cost is measured.

This plan makes documents and mock-ups only: implement no wiring. The repository is public: commit no email address, account name, machine name or absolute local path.

Your part: find out which live signals can feed the view, and write docs/monitor-3d/02-live-signals.md.

For each of the four agents, list every signal that reveals: a tool call starting, ending or failing; a resource being touched (a file read, written or searched; a URL fetched; an MCP resource); the MCP server and tool of a call; which subagent made a call; a wait for the user; session and turn start and end. For each signal give: push or poll, delay, its fields, whether it installs per user (so it covers any workspace) or per project, its cost per tool call, its stability, and the URL of its official documentation. Fetch the official documentation today; do not answer from memory.

Starting points to verify:
- Claude Code hooks: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Elicitation, SessionStart, SessionEnd, Stop. Tool events carry tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id, duration_ms, agent_id inside a subagent, and an mcp_server object. MCP tools are named mcp__<server>__<tool>. A hook can be a command (optionally async) or an HTTP post, and a plugin can carry hooks without editing the user's settings. OpenTelemetry export is batched every few seconds. The transcript format is not a supported interface.
- Codex CLI: hooks with the same event names; codex exec --json has mcp_tool_call and file_change items.
- Grok Build: hooks with toolName and toolInput; MCP tools named <server>__<tool>.
- Antigravity: hooks with toolCall.name and toolCall.args; MCP through call_mcp_tool.
- Agent Client Protocol: tool_call has kind, status and locations, but no MCP server identity.

Then record what this repository captures today, with file and line: hook/hook.js (the KEEP list, describe(), what it appends to .entomatical/events/<card>.jsonl); Board.writeHooks in src/board.ts (which events; installed per card through --settings, so sessions the board did not start are unseen); CODEX_HOOKS in src/codex.ts; the ACP handling in src/board.ts; liveSessions in src/sessions.ts; how a change reaches a webview in src/extension.ts. An earlier read found: only PostToolUse is recorded (no start, failure or duration), nothing parses mcp__ names, and the target is an 80-character summary. You may read real lines in the main checkout's .entomatical/events/ for their shape; copy no content.

Also read, in the Entridir repository at C:/Users/rober/Documents/Dev Stuff/Entridir/Entridir (read only), godot/scripts/session_traffic.gd and claude_reader.gd: how it reads tool calls from logs and marks a status exact or inferred.

End the document with:
- A table of need against agent, each cell graded exact, derived or unavailable, with the signal used.
- A common event vocabulary with one JSON example each: session start and end, turn start and end, tool start and end (ok or failed, duration), resource touch (kind; read, write or search; path or URL), MCP call start and end (server, tool), subagent start and stop, waiting for the user. A later step builds its mock-up on it.
- The rules that turn each agent's tool arguments into resource touches, and what cannot be known (for example files changed by a shell command).
- A privacy rule: which fields are kept and which never are, since tool input can hold secrets.

Change nothing outside docs/monitor-3d/.
steps.reply: the commit id, the need-against-agent table, the names of the events in the vocabulary, anything you could not verify in official documentation, and the document's path

steps.title: Recommend how to build the 3D view
steps.goal:
Wyarden is getting a 3D view of what coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, Antigravity) are doing, live, in any VS Code workspace. The owner clicks objects in 3D; every change to information happens in ordinary VS Code UI, never in the scene. It must show the tools an agent uses, the resources it uses (files, URLs, context) as a separate class, and each call to an MCP server. It runs beside the agents, so it draws only on change and its cost is measured.

This plan makes documents and mock-ups only: implement no wiring. The repository is public: commit no email address, account name, machine name or absolute local path.

Your part: recommend how to build the 3D view, in docs/monitor-3d/03-build-approach.md.

Compare at least:
A. A web renderer in a VS Code webview tab that can float to its own window. Two variants: the existing dependency-free Canvas 2D renderer, and three.js on WebGL2.
B. A Godot 4 app in its own window, linked to a small VS Code extension bridge over loopback.
C. A Godot web export inside a webview.
D. Anything else that deserves a place.

Judge on: how a click in 3D becomes a VS Code action, and how a VS Code selection lights up in 3D; delay from event to pixel; memory, idle CPU and GPU; install and update (one extension package against a second, unsigned installer); Windows and Linux built together; VSCodium; Remote (WSL, SSH); label quality; keyboard and screen-reader access; testing (this repository drives webviews in headless Edge or Chrome over CDP, see test/); one view of every workspace across several VS Code windows; reuse of existing code; licence (this repository is GPL v3).

Evidence in the Entridir repository at C:/Users/rober/Documents/Dev Stuff/Entridir/Entridir (read only: never edit, build or run anything there, and leave its app alone):
- docs/plans/godot-port.md and godot/README.md: measured memory and CPU of its Electron and Godot builds, how the Godot build draws nothing at rest, and everything Godot made hard.
- nexus-3d/docs/research/2026-11-16-nexus-3d-infrastructure-options.md: four options, a recommended machine-wide event hub with no daemon, and open questions (WebGL2 in a webview on both systems; Canvas against three.js at 40, 200 and 1,000 nodes; what the third axis shows that 2D cannot).
- nexus-3d/docs/research/2026-11-11-live-agent-visualizers-report.md: the case against 3D. Answer it.
- nexus-3d/docs/evidence/ and nexus-3d/src/lattice.ts: the earlier 3D tab in this extension and its keyboard-focus problems between webviews.
History: that tab was removed on 25 November 2026 with the stated intent to remake it as a separate app. The owner leans towards Godot but asked for the best option. Judge on evidence. If it points away from Godot or from a separate app, say so plainly and say what he would give up.

Check current facts in official documentation today (fetch the pages): VS Code webviews (WebGL2, retainContextWhenHidden, content security policy, a floated webview reloading, Remote), Godot 4 web export and networking, low processor mode.

Measure where you can; never estimate. At least: the draw time of the Canvas renderer in nexus-3d/ui-concepts/nexus-lattice-29d4d1/scene.js at 40, 200 and 1,000 nodes in headless Edge or Chrome (median of 50 full draws). Keep the script in docs/monitor-3d/bench/ and record the method. Cite Godot's recorded figures; do not re-measure them. Where you could not measure, write 'not measured' and why.

Shape: the recommendation in the first five lines (one option; where the 3D runs; how it talks to VS Code). Then the comparison table, the conditions that would make the runner-up win, the three biggest risks with a way to reduce each, the cost of the recommendation (processes, memory, idle CPU, install steps), and what is unverified. Say what it costs to keep the event feed and the action channel independent of the renderer, so a second renderer could attach later.

Change nothing outside docs/monitor-3d/.
steps.reply: the commit id, the recommendation in two sentences, the runner-up and what would make it win, every number you measured and every one you could not, and the document's path

steps.title: Build the improved mock-ups beside the originals
steps.goal:
Wyarden is getting a 3D view of what coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, Antigravity) are doing, live, in any VS Code workspace. The owner clicks objects in 3D; every change to information happens in ordinary VS Code UI, never in the scene. It must show the tools an agent uses, the resources it uses (files, URLs, context) as a separate class, and each call to an MCP server. It runs beside the agents, so it draws only on change and its cost is measured.

This plan makes documents and mock-ups only: implement no wiring. The repository is public: commit no email address, account name, machine name or absolute local path.

Your part: build the improved mock-ups in ui-concepts/monitor-3d/, a new folder. The originals stay untouched in the Entridir repository at C:/Users/rober/Documents/Dev Stuff/Entridir/Entridir (read only), under nexus-3d/ui-concepts/. You may copy their code as a start (both repositories are GPL v3); say so in the README.

Read first, on your branch: docs/monitor-3d/01-mockup-critique.md (its numbered improvements are your work list) and docs/monitor-3d/02-live-signals.md (its event vocabulary is your data model).

Build:
1. A live model fed by events, not a script. Node classes: agent, subagent, tool, resource (file, URL, context), MCP server. A call is a link that exists while the call is open. Drop every node that no live signal can supply.
2. A feed simulator: a seeded generator that emits the vocabulary's events as a stream, with start, pause and speed, and presets for 1, 4 and 12 agents and for quiet and busy periods. The view takes events through one function, subscribe(onEvent), so real data can replace the simulator later without touching the view. Connect to nothing real.
3. The critique's must-have improvements. At least: a fixed place and a distinct silhouette for each class; status as a badge or outline, never by replacing the class colour and never by colour alone; slots that never move an existing node when another arrives or leaves; resources sized by touch count, with read and write marked apart; MCP servers at the boundary, with a visible link while a call is open; labels by level of detail; idle items folded into a +N stack.
4. Drawing only on change: no requestAnimationFrame loop at rest; one redraw per batch of events (at most 10 a second) and per camera input; a visible count of frames drawn; decorative motion off by default.
5. Interaction: a click selects. The inspector shows facts and an 'In VS Code' list of what the wiring would do (open the file, show the diff, focus the session, show the call, open the MCP configuration) as labels, not working controls. Nothing in the page edits information. The keyboard moves the selection from node to node. A legend gives shape, colour and name. A list twin of the scene serves screen readers.
6. Looks: build the concept the critique ranks first. If that is not the NEXUS lattice, add the lattice as a second look on the same model and engine, one file per look. Do not rebuild the other concepts.
7. No packages, no build step, no network. node serve.js gives a loopback-only preview, and index.html opens directly. It works at 1280x720 and at 800x600.
8. node check.js: dependency-free checks of the model, slot stability under adds and removes, no draw without a change, class separation, keyboard reachability and finite coordinates.
9. README.md: how to open it, each numbered improvement marked done or not done, and what is fictional. Save a screenshot of each look under docs/monitor-3d/img/after/ with headless Edge or Chrome (test/compile-webview-cdp.js shows how); if no browser runs, say so.

Change nothing outside ui-concepts/monitor-3d/ and docs/monitor-3d/img/after/.
steps.reply: the commit id, which looks you built, each numbered improvement as done or not done, the number of checks node check.js passed, and the command that opens the mock-ups

steps.title: Write the wiring plan and the start page
steps.goal:
Wyarden is getting a 3D view of what coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, Antigravity) are doing, live, in any VS Code workspace. The owner clicks objects in 3D; every change to information happens in ordinary VS Code UI, never in the scene. It must show the tools an agent uses, the resources it uses (files, URLs, context) as a separate class, and each call to an MCP server. It runs beside the agents, so it draws only on change and its cost is measured.

This plan makes documents and mock-ups only: implement no wiring. The repository is public: commit no email address, account name, machine name or absolute local path.

Your part: write the wiring plan, docs/monitor-3d/04-wiring-plan.md, and the start page, docs/monitor-3d/README.md. Implement nothing.

Read first, on your branch: 01-mockup-critique.md, 02-live-signals.md and 03-build-approach.md in docs/monitor-3d/, and ui-concepts/monitor-3d/ (its subscribe(onEvent) feed is the seam the wiring fills). Plan for the option that 03 recommends. If you disagree with it, add a short Dissent section and still plan for it.

The plan covers:
1. The architecture in one diagram: collectors, hub, 3D view, actions into VS Code, selection back from VS Code.
2. The event contract, version 1: schema, ids, ordering, a snapshot on connect followed by changes, limits on what is kept.
3. A collector for each agent: the signal used; how it is installed so that any workspace is covered, including sessions the board did not start (today hooks are per card, through --settings); its cost per tool call and how that stays low; what is exact, derived or missing; what the view shows when it is absent. Name the existing code each would change (hook/hook.js, Board.writeHooks in src/board.ts, CODEX_HOOKS in src/codex.ts, the ACP handling) without changing it.
4. The hub: where it runs, the transport, several VS Code windows at once, Remote, and security (loopback only, a token, redaction, the privacy rule from 02).
5. Wiring the view: replacing the simulator; packaging (the .vscodeignore allow-list, tools/vsix-check.js, the content security policy and localResourceRoots, tools/parity.js with docs/parity/FEATURES.md, licenses/ and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md for any library), or the native app's packaging if 03 chose one.
6. An action table: for each class of object, what a click, a double-click and a menu do in VS Code, with the exact command or API (open a file, vscode.diff, show a terminal, the Claude Code session link, another window's workspace), and the reverse: the active editor highlights its resource. The 3D view gets no editing controls.
7. Any workspace: what must change in the workspace gate (src/workspace.ts, repoRoot in src/extension.ts), untrusted workspaces, and what the view shows before any collector is installed.
8. A resource budget and how to measure it before and after: memory, idle CPU, frames drawn at rest (zero), delay from event to pixel.
9. Tests: recorded event files replayed into the view, webview tests over CDP, Windows and Linux together.
10. Phases. Each is a slice that can ship, with acceptance criteria, the files it touches, the checks to add to workflows/checks.json, and its size in sessions. Phase 1 is the thinnest slice end to end: one agent, with a tool call, a resource and an MCP call reaching the view, and one action reaching VS Code.
11. At most seven open decisions for the owner, each with your recommended answer.

README.md is the page the owner opens first: five lines on each result with a link (the critique, the mock-ups and how to open them, the recommendation, the wiring plan), then the decisions he must make.

Change nothing outside docs/monitor-3d/.
steps.reply: the commit id, the phases by name with their size, the open decisions with your recommended answers, and the paths of the wiring plan and the start page
